title.zh: 把“现代焦虑”当作后台耗电进程来清理
title.en: Treating Modern Anxiety as Background CPU Drain

old_assumption.zh: 下班累到连游戏都不想打、书也看不进，是因为自己懒或不够自律。
old_assumption.en: Being too drained to even enjoy games or hobbies after work means you lack discipline.

new_shift.zh: 大脑的焦虑警报系统会像死循环进程一样在后台吃光全部心理带宽；先做“进程排查”关掉虚假生存警报，行动力和松弛感会自然恢复。
new_shift.en: Chronic low-grade anxiety runs like a rogue background process eating 90% of your mental RAM—killing false survival alarms restores joy and agency faster than willpower.

zh: 我最近感觉精力被掏空，脑子里一直在后台转着这些事：[列出让你隐隐焦虑的 3 件事]。请帮我做一次“心理带宽审计”：区分哪些是真实迫近的威胁，哪些是大脑误报的虚假警报，并给每项配一个 5 分钟内的物理收尾动作。
用“原始人视角”重新审视我当下的生活状态：[简述你的现状]，帮我把现代社会制造的虚拟压力翻译成底层现实，写一段 50 字以内的冷静重置口诀。
en: My mental RAM feels maxed out by these nagging thoughts: [List 3 Worries]. Run a 'background process audit' separating real immediate threats from false alarms, and give each a 5-minute physical closure step.
Reframe my current stress—[Briefly Describe Situation]—through a grounded first-principles lens to separate real survival needs from manufactured modern pressure.

note.zh: 行为经济学研究：匮乏感与焦虑会直接征收“认知带宽税”
note.en: Behavioral economics research showing how anxiety directly taxes cognitive bandwidth

title.zh: 用“工程摩擦力设计”替代消耗意志力
title.en: Engineering Environmental Friction Instead of Willpower

old_assumption.zh: 戒掉坏习惯、养成好习惯，靠的是每天逼自己咬牙坚持和打卡。
old_assumption.en: Building good habits and breaking bad ones requires daily willpower and streak tracking.

new_shift.zh: 人的默认行为高度服从“最小阻力路径”；给坏习惯人为增加 20 秒操作摩擦、给好习惯减掉 2 个前置步骤，效果远胜过任何励志鸡汤。
new_shift.en: Human defaults follow the path of least resistance—adding 20 seconds of friction to bad habits and removing 2 setup steps from good ones beats willpower every time.

zh: 我想减少 [某个坏习惯，如睡前刷手机]，并增加 [某个好习惯，如每天运动/阅读 20 分钟]。不要给我鸡汤，请从物理空间和手机设置两个维度，设计 5 个“加摩擦/减摩擦”的硬核环境改造方案。
审视我每天下班后的固定动线：[描述你回家后的前 30 分钟]，找出导致我滑向低质量娱乐的“默认触发点”，设计一个几乎不费脑子的替换动线。
en: I want to do less [Bad Habit] and more [Good Habit]. Skip motivational advice—give me 5 concrete physical-space and device-setting tweaks that add friction to the bad default and remove friction from the good one.
Audit my post-work routine—[Describe First 30 Mins at Home]—pinpoint the default trigger leading to low-quality scrolling, and engineer an effortless replacement path.

note.zh: 选择架构（Choice Architecture）：改变环境默认选项比改变人性容易十倍
note.en: Choice architecture: redesigning defaults is 10x easier than fighting human nature

title.zh: 用“14 天微型实验”替代宏大的人生决定
title.en: Running 14-Day Micro-Experiments Instead of Big Life Bets

old_assumption.zh: 换城市、转行、开启副业或改变作息，必须先彻底想清楚再孤注一掷。
old_assumption.en: Moving cities, switching careers, or changing lifestyles requires figuring everything out before making a huge leap.

new_shift.zh: 绝大多数人生纠结都是“空想出来的”；把宏大决定压缩成一个低成本、可回滚的 14 天原型实验，亲身跑一遍拿到真实体感数据，答案立刻浮现。
new_shift.en: Most life paralysis comes from overthinking without data—shrinking big decisions into cheap, reversible 14-day prototypes gives you real lived signal fast.

zh: 我一直在纠结一个比较大的人生/生活方式选择：[描述你的纠结，如移居/自由职业/新方向]。请帮我把它压缩成一个“成本极低、完全可回滚”的 14 天微型原型实验，包含具体执行动作和 3 个评估指标。
针对我想尝试的新生活方式 [描述理想状态]，列出我目前最可能高估的幻想和最可能低估的日常麻烦，设计一次周末就能跑通的“最小现实模拟”。
en: I've been overthinking a big life choice: [Describe Choice, e.g., relocating/freelancing/new path]. Compress it into a cheap, reversible 14-day micro-experiment with daily actions and 3 clear pass/fail signals.
For the lifestyle I'm romanticizing—[Describe Lifestyle]—identify what I'm likely over-glorifying or underestimating, and design a weekend reality-check simulation.

note.zh: 用科学实验的假设-验证循环替代线性目标焦虑
note.en: Replacing rigid linear goals with small, curiosity-driven personal experiments

title.zh: 从“被动适应生活脚本”反转为“按核心诉求定制生活”
title.en: Designing Life Around Your Real Constraints Instead of Default Scripts

old_assumption.zh: 上学、工作、买房、结婚、攒钱到退休是一条默认轨道，只能顺着往前走。
old_assumption.en: Life follows a single default script—school, job, milestones, retirement—and you just adapt to it.

new_shift.zh: 远程协作与数字工具让地域、节奏和收入来源有了更多组合空间；先想清楚自己真正看重什么、讨厌什么，再反推适合自己的生活结构。
new_shift.en: Remote work and digital tools expand how you combine location, schedule, and income—start from what you genuinely value and dislike, then shape the structure around it.

zh: 帮我做一次“生活脚本盘点”：列出 3 件我目前顺理成章在做的事，看看哪些是真正符合我价值观的，哪些只是惯性或外界期待。
如果让我拥有一定程度的时间与地点自由，结合 [你的核心收入/技能方向]，设计 2 种完全不同但可行的理想生活原型。
en: Run a 'default script check' on 3 things I currently do out of habit: which ones truly fit what I care about vs. inherited expectations?
Given [Your Skill/Income Direction], sketch 2 realistic lifestyle designs that prioritize autonomy over default conventions.

note.zh: 把生活当作可调整的系统来设计，而不是不可更改的既定命运
note.en: Treating daily life as an adaptable design system rather than a fixed script

title.zh: 定期“修剪和归档”数字与物理杂物，而不是无休止囤积
title.en: Pruning and Archiving Digital & Physical Clutter Instead of Hoarding

old_assumption.zh: 收藏夹、笔记、网盘和房间里的东西留着总有一天用得上，删掉或丢掉就是浪费。
old_assumption.en: Bookmarks, notes, files, and physical items might come in handy someday—tossing or archiving them feels wasteful.

new_shift.zh: 囤积本身是有维护成本和心理噪音的；定期做“极简归档与清理”，让眼前只留下真正活跃、能产生动作的东西，清爽感会立竿见影。
new_shift.en: Hoarding carries hidden cognitive and maintenance tax—periodic pruning and archiving clears mental clutter so active items stand out.

zh: 我的 [收藏夹/笔记库/桌面/衣柜] 已经堆积了不少东西但很少回头看。帮我设计一套 20 分钟就能完成的“保留 / 归档 / 清理”三分法规则，帮我快速瘦身。
针对我总舍不得删掉的 [某类数字或实体物品]，帮我写 3 个犀利的问题，帮我判断它到底是“宝藏”还是“心理安慰剂”。
en: My [Bookmarks/Notes/Desktop/Closet] has piled up with things I rarely revisit. Give me a 20-minute 'Keep / Archive / Drop' rule to declutter fast.
For [Digital or Physical Items I Hesitate to Discard], give me 3 sharp questions to tell real future utility from sentimental hoarding.

note.zh: 数字极简主义：有意识地减少噪音，只保留高价值的工具与连接
note.en: Digital minimalism: intentionally reducing low-value noise to keep what truly matters

title.zh: 用“身体状态切换”打断脑力死循环，而不是靠硬扛
title.en: Resetting Mental Loops Through Physical State Shifts

old_assumption.zh: 脑子卡住或情绪紧绷时，应该继续坐在屏幕前盯着想通为止。
old_assumption.en: When stuck or tense mentally, stay at the screen and push through until it clicks.

new_shift.zh: 久坐、缺光和浅呼吸会让大脑维持在低效紧绷态；一次 10 分钟的快走、晒太阳、拉伸或冷水洗脸，往往比硬盯屏幕 1 小时更能打破死循环。
new_shift.en: Sitting still and shallow breathing keep the brain locked in a tense loop—a 10-minute walk, daylight, stretching, or cool water often breaks the stall faster than staring at a screen.

zh: 当我连续盯着电脑/手机太久、脑子发僵或焦躁时，请帮我设计一套“5～10 分钟室内外微重启清单”，分出适合白天和睡前的不同版本。
如何把 [你喜欢的简单身体活动，如散步/拉伸/力量训练/做饭] 变成工作与休息之间自然的“状态切换仪式”，让我不再把工作情绪带进休息时间？
en: When I've been staring at screens too long and feel stiff or mentally jammed, give me a 5–10 minute physical reset menu with daytime and evening options.
How can I turn [Simple Physical Activity, e.g., walking/stretching/cooking] into a clean transition ritual between work and off-duty time?

note.zh: 通过呼吸节奏、光照与身体运动调节自主神经状态，是成本最低的身心调节手段
note.en: Using breath cadence, light exposure, and movement to shift physiological state quickly

title.zh: 备一份“低门槛恢复清单”，别等耗尽才想起来充电
title.en: Keeping a Low-Friction Recovery Menu Before Burnout Hits

old_assumption.zh: 休息就是躺着刷短视频，或者等假期攒够了再一次性大放松。
old_assumption.en: Rest means zoning out on short feeds or waiting for a big vacation to finally recharge.

new_shift.zh: 高消耗刷屏往往越刷越空，而提前准备好的“15 分钟低门槛恢复动作”（散步、听一张专辑、做顿简单饭、见一位老友）能在疲惫早期就把电量拉回来。
new_shift.en: Endless scrolling often leaves you emptier; a pre-made menu of 15-minute low-friction restores (a walk, music, cooking, real chat) recharges you before you hit zero.

zh: 帮我建一份分档的“个人恢复菜单”：15 分钟快充档、半天放松档、周末深度充电档，要求尽量不依赖高刺激屏幕刷屏且门槛低。
当我发现自己开始烦躁、拖延、对什么都提不起劲时，帮我写 3 个“立刻能做的微小止损动作”，帮我及时踩刹车。
en: Build a tiered personal recovery menu—15-minute quick resets, half-day unwinds, and weekend recharges—low-friction and light on mind-numbing feeds.
When I notice early signs of irritability, dread, or numbness, give me 3 tiny 'circuit-breaker' actions to pause and recover early.

note.zh: 区分真正恢复精力的活动与只是麻木消磨时间的习惯，是可持续创造力的关键
note.en: Distinguishing genuine restoration from numbing habits sustains long-term energy

title.zh: “极简随手记 + 每周 15 分钟复盘”，赢过复杂的完美系统
title.en: Simple Capture + 15-Minute Weekly Review Beats Complex Systems

old_assumption.zh: 要管理好自己，必须先搭一套精巧复杂的多维看板、标签体系和每日长篇复盘。
old_assumption.en: Managing life well requires building an intricate system of dashboards, nested tags, and long daily journals.

new_shift.zh: 系统越复杂，坚持成本越高，越容易在忙乱时断掉；只留一个随时能记的入口 + 每周 15 分钟扫一眼，反而能长期跑下去。
new_shift.en: Over-engineered systems collapse the moment life gets busy—one effortless capture inbox plus a 15-minute weekly scan actually survives over years.

zh: 我以前搭过复杂系统但总坚持不下来。请帮我设计一套“不超过 3 个动作、每周只需 15 分钟”的极简个人捕捉与复盘流程。
帮我写一份每周五或周日 15 分钟就能走完的“轻复盘 4 问”，只看真正重要的进展、卡点和下周 1～2 件要事。
en: Complex systems always fizzle out for me. Design a dead-simple capture and review habit taking 3 tiny steps and 15 minutes a week.
Write a 4-question, 15-minute weekly review focused only on real wins, bottlenecks, and 1–2 priorities for next week.

note.zh: 把脑子里的杂念清出来集中处理，核心在于“低捕捉摩擦”与“周期性清空”
note.en: Externalizing loose ends works best when capture is effortless and reviews stay lightweight

title.zh: 守住每天第一块黄金时段，别一醒来就被别人的消息接管
title.en: Guarding Your First High-Focus Block Before Other People's Messages

old_assumption.zh: 早上醒来第一件事就该看手机、回消息、刷资讯，不然怕漏掉重要事。
old_assumption.en: Checking messages and feeds first thing in the morning is normal so you don't miss anything urgent.

new_shift.zh: 一旦早起第一眼就陷入他人需求和信息流，整天的注意力主权就交出去了；哪怕先留出 30～60 分钟做一件自己的事，全天掌控感都会不一样。
new_shift.en: Opening feeds and messages first hands your attention wheel to others right away—protecting even 30–60 minutes for your own priority shifts the whole day.

zh: 我每天早上容易一睁眼就看手机/回消息，导致真正想做的事被挤掉。请帮我设计一套“温和、不制造焦虑”的晨间前 45 分钟安排。
针对 [你的日常作息，如早起党/夜猫子/轮班作息]，帮我划出每天最值得保护的一段“免打扰黄金时间”，并写出对应的防打扰小规则。
en: I often check messages and feeds right away in the morning and lose my own priority block. Design a calm, realistic first-45-minute routine.
Given my schedule—[Describe Routine]—help me protect one daily focus block and set simple boundary rules so it actually sticks.

note.zh: 有意识地为深度思考划出边界，是现代生活里维持创造力与自主感的基础
note.en: Intentional boundaries around focus blocks help preserve clarity and autonomy in connected life

title.zh: 用“预设筛选标准”来拒绝，而不是每次临时纠结人情
title.en: Using Pre-Set Criteria to Say No Without Guilt

old_assumption.zh: 每次有人找帮忙、约饭或塞任务，都要现场纠结半天“拒绝会不会伤感情”。
old_assumption.en: Every request or invite requires agonizing on the spot over whether saying no will upset someone.

new_shift.zh: 现场临时决定最容易心软答应、事后后悔；提前定好“忙什么 / 什么情况下接 / 什么情况下婉拒”，拒绝就成了顺理成章的规则而不是针对某个人。
new_shift.en: Deciding ad hoc invites people-pleasing and later regret—pre-set criteria turn 'no' into a clear priority rule rather than a personal rejection.

zh: 我经常在 [帮人忙/接临时任务/社交邀约] 上不好意思拒绝，最后把自己累垮。请帮我写 3 套不同语气（温和礼貌/真诚坦率/明确边界）的婉拒模板。
帮我定一套“个人精力红绿灯规则”：什么情况绿灯答应、黄灯延后、红灯直接婉拒。
en: I often struggle to say no to [Favors/Last-Minute Tasks/Invites] and end up stretched thin. Write 3 natural ways to decline (warm, direct, firm) without over-apologizing.
Help me create a simple green/yellow/red rule for incoming requests based on my current bandwidth and priorities.

signals.name: Essentialism — Disciplined Pursuit of Less (Greg McKeown)

note.zh: 把精力集中到少数真正重要的事上，前提是拥有清晰且不内耗的拒绝机制
note.en: Focusing on what truly matters depends on clear, low-guilt boundaries around everything else

title.zh: 设一个“睡前 30 分钟关机缓冲”，别把白天刺激直接带进床上
title.en: Creating a 30-Minute Evening Wind-Down Before Sleep

old_assumption.zh: 困了往床上一躺就能立刻睡着，睡前刷手机、想工作或看刺激内容无所谓。
old_assumption.en: You can fall straight asleep the moment your head hits the pillow even after late screens or work thoughts.

new_shift.zh: 大脑需要一个从“高速运转/高光刺激”降速到“放松准备入睡”的缓冲带；留出 20～30 分钟低刺激收尾，睡眠质量和第二天精神都会明显改善。
new_shift.en: The brain needs a ramp-down from high stimulation and work loops—a 20–30 minute low-key wind-down improves sleep quality and next-day clarity.

zh: 我晚上经常因为 [刷手机/脑子还转着工作或杂事] 导致睡不沉或晚睡。请帮我设计一套 25 分钟以内的“睡前降噪收尾流程”，简单、可坚持。
帮我写一份“睡前脑内清空清单（Brain Dump）”的 3 个小问题，把明天要做的事记下来，让自己安心放下。
en: My evenings often get derailed by [Late Scrolling or Racing Thoughts], hurting sleep. Design a calm, realistic 25-minute wind-down routine.
Give me 3 quick 'brain-dump' questions before bed to capture tomorrow's loose ends so I can mentally clock out.

note.zh: 降低晚间光线与信息刺激、给大脑留出缓冲时间，是改善睡眠最稳妥的基础动作
note.en: Dimming evening light and mental stimulation gives the nervous system room to settle for sleep

title.zh: 用“阶段主题词”替代死板的 Flag，允许计划随现实长出新样子
title.en: Using Seasonal Themes Instead of Rigid Resolutions

old_assumption.zh: 定目标就要列一长串具体 KPI 和死板打卡表，没全完成就是失败。
old_assumption.en: Good planning means a rigid checklist of targets—missing items feels like falling behind.

new_shift.zh: 现实变化很快，死板的 KPI 容易让人中途放弃；一个清晰的阶段“主题词”（比如“精简与沉淀 / 轻装试错 / 专注交付”）既能指明方向，又留有调整空间。
new_shift.en: Rigid resolutions break when life shifts—a clear seasonal theme (like 'simplify & ship' or 'low-stakes experiments') guides choices while staying adaptable.

zh: 结合我接下来 [3 个月 / 半年 / 一年] 的生活与工作重点：[简述现状与期望]。请帮我提炼 2 个贴切的“阶段主题词”，并说明在日常做选择时怎么用它做判断。
帮我把一份原本有点死板、让人有压力的计划：[简述计划]，改造成更有弹性、聚焦核心方向的阶段主题与 2～3 个关键里程碑。
en: Based on my next [Quarter, Half-Year, or Year]—[Briefly Describe Context & Hopes]—propose 2 meaningful themes and show how to use them as everyday decision filters.
Reframe this rigid checklist—[Describe Plan]—into an adaptable seasonal theme with 2–3 high-signal milestones.

signals.name: Yearly / Seasonal Themes (CGP Grey / Ness Labs)

note.zh: 以方向与主题引导行动，比死守僵化清单更容易在变化中保持推进
note.en: Directional themes guide daily trade-offs without the brittle all-or-nothing trap of rigid checklists

title.zh: 把健康习惯做成“顺手就能做 5 分钟”的小动作，而不是高难度打卡
title.en: Making Healthy Habits a 5-Minute Default Instead of an All-or-Nothing Streak

old_assumption.zh: 运动、拉伸、喝水或早起要么一次练足一小时、严格执行，要么干脆算今天没练。
old_assumption.en: Fitness, mobility, or healthy routines count only if done in full sessions—otherwise it feels like skipping altogether.

new_shift.zh: 忙乱或疲惫时，高门槛计划最容易断掉；把“5 分钟活动/伸展/出门走走”设成底线，既保住节奏又不会因为偶尔偷懒而全盘放弃。
new_shift.en: Ambitious routines break on busy days—setting a 5-minute baseline (a quick stretch, walk, or mobility break) keeps momentum alive without all-or-nothing guilt.

zh: 我平时久坐或作息容易乱，想把 [某项健康习惯，如活动肩颈/快走/规律作息] 变成轻松的日常默认项。请帮我设计一个“忙时 5 分钟保底版 + 闲时正常版”。
针对我最容易偷懒或中断的时段：[填时段]，设计 2 个几乎不需要换衣服或额外准备的微动作。
en: I sit a lot or get pulled off track and want [Health Habit, e.g., stretching/walking/consistent sleep] to feel effortless. Give me a 5-minute minimum floor and a normal-day version.
For [Time of Day When Routines Slip], suggest 2 low-prep physical habits that require zero gear or hassle.

note.zh: 保留极低门槛的“保底版本”，能显著降低中断后的重启阻力
note.en: Keeping a tiny minimum floor makes habits far easier to sustain through busy stretches

title.zh: 把社交精力留给“聊得来、不消耗人”的少数深度连接
title.en: Investing Social Energy in Low-Drain, High-Trust Connections

old_assumption.zh: 社交圈子越大越好，逢场作戏、应酬或勉强维持关系是一种必要付出。
old_assumption.en: Bigger networks are always better, and obliging draining social circles is just part of adulthood.

new_shift.zh: 个人社交带宽有限；把时间和情绪留给真正同频、相处轻松、能互相滋养的少数人，比维系十个客套关系更有获得感。
new_shift.en: Social bandwidth is finite—investing in a few energizing, low-friction relationships beats maintaining a crowd that leaves you drained.

zh: 帮我梳理一下我目前的日常社交与互动：[简述现状]，看看哪些互动真正让我觉得轻松、有启发，哪些更多是习惯性消耗。
如果我想和一位很久没联系但很投缘的朋友恢复轻量联系，帮我写 2 条自然、没有压力的破冰消息。
en: Help me reflect on my current social energy—[Brief Context]: which interactions leave me recharged vs. drained out of habit?
Draft 2 warm, low-pressure messages to reconnect with a friend I haven't spoken to in a while.

note.zh: 有意识地把精力倾斜给核心连接，能提升日常情绪质量与安全感
note.en: Prioritizing deep, low-friction ties supports emotional steadiness and genuine connection

title.zh: 一团乱麻时先做“减法”，砍掉 70% 暂时不致命的事
title.en: Subtracting 70% of Non-Urgent Load When Feeling Overwhelmed

old_assumption.zh: 事情堆得越多、越乱，越要咬牙把所有清单都排满、一起扛下来。
old_assumption.en: When everything piles up and feels overwhelming, push harder and pack more onto the list to catch up.

new_shift.zh: 过载时硬扛只会越做越乱；先挑出今天真正必须推进的 1～2 件事，其余延后、砍掉或暂放，大脑立刻就能喘口气并重新动起来。
new_shift.en: Pushing harder under overload often stalls momentum—picking 1–2 things that truly matter today and parking the rest restores clarity and traction.

zh: 我现在手头事情很多、有点乱或有点累：[列出你目前担心的 3-5 件事]。请帮我做一次“减法梳理”：挑出今天最值得先做的一件小事，其余先排出优先级或延后。
当我感觉负荷拉满、什么都不想动时，帮我写一段简短的“降维重启步骤”，帮我先稳住节奏。
en: I have a lot on my plate and feel stretched or scattered: [List 3–5 Things]. Help me subtract—pick 1 small priority to move today and sequence or defer the rest.
When overload makes everything feel heavy, give me a calm step-by-step reset to regain footing without guilt.

note.zh: 在精力紧绷时主动做减法、聚焦少数关键点，往往比硬撑更能恢复推进感
note.en: Deliberately subtracting non-essentials restores focus and forward motion when stretched thin

title.zh: 日程里故意留出“缓冲留白”，别把每一分钟都排死
title.en: Leaving Buffer Slack in Your Schedule Instead of Packing Every Slot

old_assumption.zh: 把时间表排得满满当当才算充实、高效，留白等于浪费时间。
old_assumption.en: Packing every hour back-to-back means high productivity; unscheduled gaps feel like wasted time.

new_shift.zh: 现实总会有突发状况和状态起伏；没有留白的日程一旦延迟就会全线崩盘，留出一点缓冲空间，反而能从容应对变化、保持长期节奏。
new_shift.en: Real life has delays and energy swings—back-to-back schedules domino into stress, while intentional buffer slack keeps your pace steady and adaptable.

zh: 我平时容易把日程或待办排得太满，一有突发事就打乱节奏：[简述你的日常安排]。请帮我设计一种“留出缓冲白”的排程方式。
在 [你的工作或生活节奏] 中，怎么自然地给突发情况或状态调整留出一点弹性空间？
en: I tend to pack schedules tightly and get thrown off when unexpected things pop up: [Brief Routine]. Suggest a practical way to build buffer slack into my week.
In [Your Work or Life Rhythm], how can I leave healthy margin for surprises and energy shifts without feeling behind?

note.zh: 适当的留白与缓冲能吸收日常摩擦，让长期节奏更稳健、不易透支
note.en: Intentional margin absorbs everyday friction and keeps long-term pace sustainable

title.zh: 允许自己偶尔“无聊发呆”，别用高刺激内容填满每一秒缝隙
title.en: Allowing Quiet Boredom Instead of Patching Every Gap with High Stimulation

old_assumption.zh: 排队、等车、睡前或放空时没事干就是无聊，赶紧掏出手机刷点东西才充实。
old_assumption.en: Unoccupied moments in lines, commutes, or downtime feel like wasted time—grabbing a feed fills the gap.

new_shift.zh: 持续高刺激会让大脑对日常麻木、灵感也难以冒头；留出几分钟不带输入的发呆或散步，常是好想法和松弛感的起点。
new_shift.en: Constant high-stimulation feeds dull baseline enjoyment and crowd out mind-wandering—quiet, input-free minutes often spark real ideas and calm.

zh: 盘点我每天有哪些“本来可以轻松放空几分钟”的碎片空档（如等电梯/通勤/睡前/休息间隙），却习惯性拿手机填满：[简述你的习惯]。帮我设计 3 个不带屏幕输入的轻替代。
如果我每天刻意留出 10 分钟“零信息输入”的安静时段，怎么安排才最自然、最不容易变成新的打卡负担？
en: Spot 3 everyday gaps (waiting, commuting, breaks) where I reflexively reach for a screen instead of letting my mind rest: [Brief Context]. Suggest low-friction, input-free alternatives.
How can I carve out 10 quiet, input-free minutes a day naturally without turning it into another rigid chore?

note.zh: 适度的无输入留白有助于大脑整合信息与产生创造性联结
note.en: Unstructured, low-input downtime supports reflection, calm, and creative connections

title.zh: 让 AI 帮你“压力测试选项”，而不是替你替自己做决定
title.en: Using AI to Stress-Test Choices Rather Than Outsource Your Judgment

old_assumption.zh: 纠结或拿不定主意时，直接让 AI 替我选一个或给标准答案最省事。
old_assumption.en: When torn or uncertain, having AI pick an option or hand over a neat answer feels like the fastest relief.

new_shift.zh: 生活与选择里的权重、代价和喜好只有你自己能承担；让 AI 帮拆盲区、列反方、算代价，但最终拍板和承担后果的权柄留在自己手里，才不会越用越虚。
new_shift.en: Trade-offs, personal stakes, and tastes belong to you—let AI expose blindspots and test assumptions, while keeping final judgment and ownership in your hands.

zh: 我正在 [A 选项 vs B 选项] 之间纠结：[简述两个选项与你的顾虑]。不要替我做决定，请帮我分别列出选 A 和选 B 最容易忽略的代价与前提。
针对我目前的一个重要选择：[简述选择]，帮我提出 3 个直击内心真实偏好与底线的追问，帮我自己看清更想要什么。
en: I'm weighing [Option A vs. Option B]: [Context & Concerns]. Don't pick for me—surface the hidden trade-offs and assumptions behind each choice.
For [Decision I'm Facing], ask me 3 pointed questions about my real priorities and limits so I can make the call clearly.

note.zh: 借助外部视角看清利弊，同时守住自身判断与选择责任，是更稳健的决策姿势
note.en: Using outside perspectives to see trade-offs while keeping judgment and ownership intact
